subject: botany_2
question_text: What is the cross between the F1 progeny and the homozygous recessive parent called? How is it useful?

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.42, printed question 82. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Examiner audit revision (2026-09-05): the first s1_name mistake called 'back cross' an error, although a cross made to a parent is a back cross; it and the margin note now say the asked-for name is the test cross, the back cross made to the homozygous recessive parent. Whether the wider term back cross is itself accepted on the paper is still for a Telangana IPE teacher to rule.

insider_note: One word for the name, one sentence for the use. The word GENOTYPE has to appear in the second half.

steps.label: The name
steps.margin_note: One line. The name asked for is the test cross, not the wider term back cross.
lines: Such a cross is called a TEST CROSS.
steps.why: The cross has a name of its own because it is a deliberate test rather than an ordinary breeding step.
common_mistakes: Answering only 'back cross'. This cross is made to a parent, so it is a back cross as well, but the name asked for is TEST CROSS — the back cross made to the homozygous RECESSIVE parent.
Calling it a monohybrid cross. That names the number of characters, not the purpose.
steps.memory_tip: It is a test, so it is called a test cross.

steps.label: Its use
steps.margin_note: Purpose plus both outcomes. Five lines.

lines.text: It reveals the GENOTYPE behind a dominant

lines: It is used to determine the GENOTYPE of the test
organism: whether it is homozygous or
steps.why: The recessive parent contributes nothing visible, so every offspring displays the allele it got from the unknown parent.
common_mistakes: Saying it finds the phenotype. The phenotype is already visible.
Giving no ratios. The two outcomes are what make it useful.
steps.memory_tip: All dominant means pure; half recessive means hybrid.
